author: ojiudezue
title: Oji's phantom arrivals came from a re-added iPad tracker; step 8 relies on the stale-source rule and the iPad is removed again
summary: The step 8 D0b probe found 29 of Oji's 33 arrivals that passed the 15-minute absence gate had no body in the house, with absences up to ~5 h, so no away threshold could filter them. A follow-up traced every one (and all 18 of his short flaps) to device_tracker.okosisipadmini6_2: HA's person entity lets a non-GPS tracker that reads home win over GPS, and the iPad sitting at home flipped person.oji_udezue home. The existing lock-regime stale-source rule (tracker did not change at the edge, >10 s) separated them perfectly: 29/29 phantoms stale, 0/32 real arrivals stale. The iPad had been removed on 10-18 but was back in person.oji_udezue; the operator said 'Remove it' and it was removed via person/update with a backup.
why: The step 8 plan already required a non-stale source, but nobody had measured whether that rule caught this failure. Measuring first turned a proposed new 'body test' operator question into a confirmation that existing code suffices, and exposed a regressed HA config the operator had already ruled on.
alternatives_considered: A new body test at +60/+180 s (BLE room or census presence) before arrival actions
A longer absence threshold (no value separates real from phantom: Oji's real returns were 1,814-428,382 s away)
Keep the iPad and rely only on the stale rule (rejected by operator; other person.* readers such as HVAC and HA automations do not apply it)
implications: Any new arrival consumer must read the residency record's source_stale, not raw person.* edges. person.oji_udezue tracker membership can silently regress (re-pair or manual add); a trip-wire on person tracker lists, or a periodic check, would catch it next time.
revisit_trigger: Phantom arrivals reappear in D0b-style probes, or a person.* entity gains a tracker that stays home while the person leaves.
